R1 -> Two 1000 ohm resistors in parallel
Connect it to a USB cable
Connect GND, D+, and D- to USB cable
Step down 5V power to 3.3V using 1000 ohm x 3 resistors
ChatGPT does not recommend a voltage divider circuit
Multimeter, short lengths of fine wire, flux.
Mount the regulator on a tiny perfboard:
Install an AuthenTec AES1610 OEM driver so it appears under Biometric devices. Then enroll via Windows (or use OEM utility).
A small 3.3 V regulator module (AP2112-3.3, MCP1700-3.3, MIC5504-3.3, etc.; 150–300 mA is plenty). AMS1117-3.3 also works but runs warm.
Two capacitors as per your regulator’s datasheet (typ. 10 µF on IN and OUT, plus 0.1 µF ceramics close to the module).
Identify the four pads on the module
USB red (5 V) → VIN of the regulator.
Add the input/output caps right at the pins.
A very common order (from one side to the other) is: GND – D– – D+ – 3V3.
GND: continuity to big ground copper/shield, and to the USB shield can.
+3.3 V: goes to decoupling caps to ground (you’ll see/measure a cap there).
The remaining two are D–/D+; they run into a tiny ESD diode part near the connector. If unsure which is which, you can swap later—no damage will occur.
If they aren’t labeled, confirm with a meter:
Prepare the USB cable. Cut, strip, and tin the four wires. Keep white/green twisted for as long as possible.
Regulator VOUT (3.3 V) will go to the module’s 3V3 pad.
Module GND → USB black (and regulator GND).
Leave USB red isolated from the module (it only feeds the regulator).
If there’s a cable shield/drain, tie it to GND near the connector (optional but nice).
If it shows “Unknown device” and you’re certain the 3.3 V is stable: swap D+ and D– and try again.
Do not feed 5 V straight into the board. You’ll use the USB red wire only to power the 3.3 V regulator.
Strain relief and insulate (heat-shrink/hot glue) so nothing can short.
Bench-check first: With USB unplugged, verify no shorts between 3.3 V and GND.
Plug into a USB port → measure the regulator: you should see ~3.30 V at the module.
Windows Device Manager should enumerate an AuthenTec device (or “Unknown” if drivers are missing).
Keep the D+/D– pair short (<15 cm of free wire) and twisted the whole way.
Current draw is typically <100 mA, but pick a regulator with comfortable headroom.
If your module originally had two power pads (+3V and +3VS), the 4-pin version usually ties them; if you ever see two separate 3.3-V pads, bridge them and feed both.
Don’t connect the module until you’ve verified the regulator outputs 3.3 V with the cable plugged into USB.
A spare USB-A cable you can cut (wires: red=+5 V, white=D–, green=D+, black=GND, plus shield).
